text:
security-bot: Alert: S3 object s3://redwood-backups/2026-03-20/dump.tar.gz matched regex for API keys (possible ingest/api key). Confidence: medium. Detected by storage-scan job.

kari (security): I pulled the object quickly, looks like a compressed log archive. @jordan can you confirm if that bucket is internal-only and how this file was generated?

jordan (infra): That bucket is internal backups, not public. Backup job runs from backup-runner IAM role. We have lifecycle policies but the object path matches an ad-hoc export job from eng data-tool last week.

samir (oncall): Copying the grep we ran inside the dump: `zgrep -E \"(sk_live|ingest_live|api_key=)\" dump/*.log | head -n 5` returned 3 hits with tokens that look like service.ingest keys.

mike (eng): Uh — that sounds like an ingest key embedded in logs from the ingest-service. We recently added expanded debug logging for failed auth; looks like a code path accidentally printed the full key. I'm owner of that service, will triage.

kari (security): Action items: 1) Revoke the exposed key immediately. 2) Identify which customers (if any) used that key. 3) Rotate keys where needed and check CI/deployments for references. 4) Audit S3 access and who pulled the dump. 5) Postmortem and notify leadership.

jordan (infra): I can revoke the key if you give me the key id. Also locking down the bucket ACLs while we investigate. Will also set a retention/immutable flag on that object to prevent accidental re-exposure while we triage.

mike (eng): Key id is ingest_live_ak_7xx3 (from the log). That key is provisioned via internal KMS-backed secrets manager and rotated monthly. I will check the service repo for recent changes that might have logged it.

opsbot: Incident created: #INC-2026-0319-01 - \"Ingest key leaked in backup dump\". Pager duty alert sent to oncall.

samir (oncall): I'm running `aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue=ingest_live_ak_7xx3 --start-time 2026-03-14 --end-time 2026-03-20` to see usage. Will post results in 10m.

kari (security): Also run `aws iam generate-service-last-accessed-details` for the principal that owns the key. We need to know if it was used externally.

mike (eng): Quick update: found the debug change in `ingest-service` commit 4f2a2d that added `log.debug("auth token=%s", token)` inside the auth middleware. That was behind a feature flag but somehow enabled in the backup job that performed a dry run. Rolling back that change in staging now.

jordan (infra): Bucket ACLs temporarily set to private, public access blocked. PUT/GET logs show only internal IPs accessed the object. No 403s or public GETs in CloudTrail.

samir (oncall): CloudTrail lookup shows the key was used from our internal pool only — no calls from external IPs. Last use: 2026-03-18 11:22 UTC from ingest-service instance i-0abc.

kari (security): Good — no confirmed customer compromise so far, but we should assume key leaked. Recommend immediate key revocation and rotate. Also: verify if backups were ever exported to external storage or shared with third parties.

mike (eng): I'll generate a new ingest key and wire it through the secrets manager. Need a short maintenance window to restart the service with the new key. ETA 20m.

jordan (infra): If you want zero-downtime, we can add the new key as a secondary key and do a rolling restart so both keys are accepted for 10 minutes. Then remove the old key.

mike (eng): Doing that. Creating new key: `secretsctl create --name ingest-api-key --kms=kms://alias/redwood` returning id ingest_live_ak_9ab2. I'll push to secrets manager and call for rolling restart.

ci-bot: CI check: grep found 2 references to ingest_live_ak_7xx3 in repo `data-tool` and `ingest-service` — creating PRs to remove persisted values.

kari (security): Whoever pushed the dump — please attach context: why was a backup pulled and archived with logs included. We need to update our backup sanitization process to scrub secrets before archiving.

mike (eng): Confirmed PRs incoming. I will also add sanitizer to the backup pipeline: run `gitleaks` or `redact-logs` step before tar.

jordan (infra): Audit note: enabling S3 object lock on the backup bucket is not ideal for this case. We'll instead implement pre-archive scrubbing and enforce object encryption + no public access. Also creating a policy to block uploading archives containing `*.log` without a scan tag.

samir (oncall): Revocation done at 2026-03-20T14:12Z: old key ingest_live_ak_7xx3 disabled. No errors observed after rolling restart; 200s for health checks.

kari (security): Next steps: - Postmortem (owner: mike) due EOD tomorrow. - Add sanitizer to backup-runner (owner: jordan). - Automated secret-scan on S3 create events to detect future leaks (owner: security infra). - Notify legal if we find customer identifiers tied to leaked key (blocked until we have evidence).

mike (eng): Will own postmortem and follow-ups. Thanks everyone.

opsbot: Incident #INC-2026-0319-01 updated: severity lowered to P2 after containment.

kari (security): Closing note: good containment, no external usage seen. Please follow the rotation checklist and include timeline in postmortem. :white_check_mark:
